objective: Every reply's post view carries the post it replies to, one level deep, so a reply card can show its parent without a request per card; and the feed includes replies that have at least one like.
acceptance_criteria: Start gate: FEED-001 has merged to main, since both change the feed's post selection. Test-first: commit the failing tests alone before the implementation; the implementation commit edits no test.

Every PostView (GET /feed, GET /feed/thread/{id}, GET /feed/history, GET /search/posts) carries replied_post and replied_post_deleted. On a reply, replied_post is the PostView of its parent, with the parent's own counts and viewer flags; on every other post it is null and replied_post_deleted is false.
One level deep: a replied_post's own replied_post is always null, and so is its reposted_post unless the next criterion applies.

When the parent is a plain repost, replied_post is the view of the post that repost stands for, the same rule the post card already applies to a plain repost. A quote repost parent is the quote itself, with its reposted_post null (the depth cut).

A parent its owner deleted gives replied_post null and replied_post_deleted true. A parent hidden because its author is deactivated or soft-deleted gives replied_post null and replied_post_deleted false. A reply's own visibility rules are unchanged.
Building the views stays batched: the statement count for a page of 2 posts equals that for a page of 20, with replies, their parents and reposts mixed in, pinned by a statement-counting test.
assemble_post_views reads parents through app.posts.service's existing public reads (posts_by_ids, deleted_post_ids), or a new public function there, never posts' tables directly (Connection rule).

backend/openapi.json and frontend/src/api/schema.d.ts are regenerated, and every frontend fixture that builds a PostView sets both new fields, so the frontend suite compiles and passes unchanged in behaviour.

GET /feed, for guests and signed-in viewers alike, includes a reply exactly when it has at least one like, counted as the like_count its PostView reports. It is selected under the same author and mention rules as top-level posts, at its own id in the newest-first order: a like moves nothing. A reply with no likes never appears, and one whose last like is removed drops out on the next read. Top-level posts and reposts are unchanged, liked or not.
With liked replies mixed in, the before_id cursor still neither repeats nor skips a post across pages, and next_before_id keeps its full-page rule.

A migration adds an index on post_likes(post_id), which the like check reads; the PR states the feed query's plan before and after on the dev database. GET /feed/history, /feed/thread and search are unchanged in what they select.
wiki/CodeContext/Modules/0x06-feed.md records the two fields beside reposted_post and the liked-replies rule; 0x03-posts.md records the index.
